turns.t: Margaret Pemberton? Date of birth the fourth of March, nineteen fifty-one?
That's me. I've brought my diary, if that's all right. I've been writing it down since the start.
Brilliant, that saves time. Leg cramps, I see from the booking. Walk me through it.
Right. I get terrible cramps in my calves at night, mostly the left, waking me up around two in the morning. They've been going on for six weeks.
Six weeks. How often, according to the diary?
Let me see. Three or four nights a week. Last week it was four, Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday.
How bad are they when they hit?
Severe. I have to get out of bed and stand on the cold floor. I'd put it at eight out of ten, and there's a sore ache left behind the next day.
Anything that sets them off, anything that helps?
They're worse after a day of gardening. Stretching the calf against the wall is the only thing that eases it.
Good detail. Anything else going on with the legs?
My ankles swell by the evening. And I'm tired, a heavy sort of tired, which is new since the autumn.
Swollen ankles and tiredness, noted. Now, a few safety questions. Any chest pain, or shortness of breath on the stairs?
No chest pain. No shortness of breath either, I did the stairs at the library yesterday without any trouble.
Good. Any numbness in the legs, or weakness, like your leg giving way?
No numbness, and no weakness. Just the cramps.
Right. Tablets. What are you taking at the moment?
The amlodipine, 5 mg once a day in the morning, for the blood pressure. And the water tablet, furosemide, 40 mg, once a day as well.
Okay, and do you take them every day?
Every morning, regularly, without fail. I have a pill box with the days on it.
Good. Any allergies to medicines?
Penicillin. I get a rash, it came up all over my chest when I was about thirty. I've avoided it ever since.
Penicillin and a rash, I'll flag that. Any other medical conditions apart from the blood pressure?
Osteoarthritis in my knees. And migraines, though they stopped after the menopause.
Blood pressure, osteoarthritis, migraines. Any operations?
The gallbladder came out about ten years ago. And I had a right knee replacement in 2019, which was a great success.
And in the family, any big illnesses?
My father had a stroke. My mother had type 2 diabetes for years.
Thank you. Do you smoke or drink?
I stopped smoking twenty years ago. A glass of wine with dinner, no more. I'm a retired teacher, so I'm very good at following rules.
That makes my job easier. Any trouble with your waterworks, passing urine?
No, that's all normal. Although I notice the water tablet makes me go a lot in the morning.
Expected with that tablet. I'll do your observations and then take a look at your legs.
Blood pressure is 148 over 86. Pulse 72 beats per minute. Temperature 36.6 degrees. Oxygen saturation 97 percent. And your weight is 78 kilograms.
My blood pressure is usually a bit lower than that at home. I've got those numbers in the diary too.
I'll look at the diary afterwards. Lie back, I'm checking both lower legs now.
There's mild swelling around both ankles. No redness or warmth in either calf, and the pulses at the feet are present.
Is that good?
Reassuring. Here's my thinking. The cramps are most likely related to your water tablet, which can wash out potassium and magnesium. But I can't rule out a circulation problem in the legs as well.
And the swelling?
Amlodipine can cause some of that too, so it may be both tablets. I'm not changing anything today until I have bloods.
Understood.
I'd like to order a blood test for your potassium and kidney function, and a separate magnesium level. You can have both done this morning.
Fine. Fasting?
No need. I'll also arrange an ECG, because low potassium can affect the heart rhythm. The nurse can do it straight after the bloods.
Is there anything about my heart I should worry about?
Nothing that I've heard or seen so far. This is to be careful. If the swelling doesn't settle, we'll consider an ultrasound scan of the leg veins.
All right.
For the cramps themselves, stretch the calves before bed, keep your fluids up through the day, and bring the diary next time.
I'll add a column for the stretching. And I wanted to mention, looking at the diary again, I did actually miss the amlodipine on Tuesday and Thursday last week.
Thanks for being honest. Try to take it with breakfast every morning so it's tied to something. Don't double up when you miss one.
Noted.
I'll see you again in ten days to go through the results.
Ten days. I'll make the appointment at the desk.
Good. Off you go to the lab.
Thank you, doctor.
Goodbye, Mrs Pemberton.
